current.text: LeBron James left the Lakers for the Sixers, and Rui Hachimura appears to be gone too. Doncic and Reaves are the remaining core. The Lakers also added Collin Sexton.
He re-signed with the Lakers for 4 years and 185 million. His salary tripled.
He is a projected starter next to Doncic, Grimes, Thybulle and Kessler.
With LeBron gone, his usage should rise and his assist rate most of all. Experts expect a step forward.
He is projected for about 28% usage, 36 minutes and 6 assists, which fits around picks 15 to 18. With 30% usage and 7.5 assists he could be a first-round player.

Experts disagree on his ceiling. Most see first-round upside and a top-12 finish as possible, and Josh ranks him above Donovan Mitchell. One Lakers preview says he is fine at the end of round 2 but should not go in round 1, and Josh thinks Jamal Murray is likelier to finish top 12.
His draft cost is rising. Recent mocks took him at picks 12 to 14, and he is moving into the early second round.
His ESPN rank (around 50, later moved to 64) is far too low. He is the best Lakers target, especially on ESPN.
In auctions Josh values him at about 36 USD. A 40 USD price is an overpay.
His Yahoo rank around 20 is good value in category leagues. In points leagues he is closer to a third-round player.
His efficiency could fall this season. It already dipped toward the end of last season.
If Luka Doncic misses time, Reaves would run around 32% usage and play like a first-round player.
If the Lakers are not working, he could be the player they trade, even if he plays well.
The Lakers have the second most back-to-backs in the league. Their playoff schedule with a March 28 end is 3-4-3 games, in the bottom half of the league.

durable.text: He takes many free throws at a great percentage. He also adds points, threes and assists.
Turnovers are his weakest category and a clear outlier. Josh expects more turnovers from him than from Jamal Murray.
He gives little in steals and blocks.
Experts disagree on his FG%. One calls his efficiency excellent. Others say it can be a problem and expect it to trail Jamal Murray's.
Soft tissue injuries are a risk for him.
His value depends on his role. He played like a second-round player next to only one of LeBron or Luka, and at a top-12 level when LeBron was out. Next to both he fell to third option.
He is a better category league player than points league player.
Andy sees his game as very similar to Luka Doncic's and thinks he adds little that Luka does not.

note: Yahoo values him at 33 USD and drafters pay about 29 USD. ESPN prices him much lower (15 USD value, 23.5 USD average cost), and he cost 25 USD in our league last season. Josh's 36 USD value with 40 USD as an overpay is a sensible ceiling for us, since recent mocks now take him at picks 12 to 14. His elite FT% on volume plus points, threes and assists suit punt TO and FT%-strong builds, but the many back-to-backs and his groin history add risk. Early on, check whether his usage and assists really jump without LeBron and whether his FG% holds near 48%.
